## E4 (tailnet) + E5 (memory/backup) — inline findings, 2026-07-15

### E4 tailnet mechanism (the piece E3 made critical — fleet unreachable via vmnet ⇒ hermes-in-container needs tailscale)
- **`/dev/net/tun` IS present** in the apple/container guest (`crw------- 10,200`; kernel 6.18.15) — real-TUN is theoretically available (obsoletes highpost's "userspace-only" premise).
- **Real TUN FAILS without caps**: `tailscaled --tun=tun0` → `tstun.New("tun0"): operation not permitted` (needs CAP_NET_ADMIN to create the iface). `container run --cap-add NET_ADMIN` IS supported and would fix it — BUT NET_ADMIN is not in the proxy's safeCaps, so nested agent containers can't get it (only the top-level agent container, created by the deployment, can).
- **Userspace-networking WORKS out of the box**: `tailscaled --tun=userspace-networking` runs, magicsock inits, `tailscale status` = "Logged out" (daemon up, ready to auth). Only non-fatal UDP-buffer-size warnings ("impacts throughput only"). This is the viable path for hermes-in-a-container — no caps needed.
- **Full join + reach-metal test: PENDING a user-gated ephemeral `tag:hermes` authkey** (not minting against the shared tailnet unilaterally). Mechanism is proven up to auth.
- Kill matrix (lifecycle recovery) still to run (destructive — deferred until other live experiments quiesce).

### E5 memory — per-VM backing process (clean instrument; host-wide wired is unusable here — rapid-mlx wires ~20GB and dominates it)
- Each apple/container micro-VM is backed by a host `com.apple.Virtualization.VirtualMachine.xpc` process; its RSS is the clean footprint.
- **Measured idle overhead: ~336–356 MB RSS per micro-VM** (3 samples: the 2G alpine machine ≈356 MB, two 1G containers ≈336–341 MB). This is OUR primary measurement — replaces the unsourced ~200 MB figure (real number is higher, ~340 MB idle).
- **A 2G-configured machine holds only ~356 MB idle** — apple/container does NOT pre-wire the full `--memory` (grows as the guest touches pages), unlike tart which wires the full 4 GiB. Favorable for the migration's memory story.
- Daemons are negligible: apiserver 20 MB, socktainer 27 MB, proxy 15 MB; plugin helpers (runtime-linux 37 MB, network-vmnet 13 MB, core-images 52 MB) ~115 MB total.
- **Deferred**: the no-page-release SHRINK behavior (my balloon test was contaminated — /dev/shm capped at 64 MB so `dd` wrote 0 bytes, and host-wired is rapid-mlx-noisy) and 24h growth. Clean quantification needs a quiet host or a per-VM-process time series; the Apple-documented "freed pages not relinquished" stands as the qualitative expectation. Baseline series started at `~/.yclaw/spike-container/soak/mem-samples.tsv`.

### E5 backup — restic file-level model (DECISIVE)
- **Bind-mount host path = PASS**: files written inside a container via `-v <hostdir>:/data` appear DIRECTLY on the host as normal files (`session1.json`, `sub/nested.txt`) — restic file-level backup works exactly as it does for the live `hermesstate` share today (`just backup` over `~/.yclaw/state`).
- **Named volume = opaque**: `container volume` is a single ext4 disk image (`.../volumes/<name>/volume.img`, `format: ext4`, 512G sparse) — restic would back up the whole opaque blob, no file-level dedup/browse/restore. Confirms the memo: **the migration must bind-mount hermes state, never use named volumes.**

Cleaned test artifacts (e5-testvol deleted, sim dir removed); apiserver up; zero 64.x in container nets.
